title: UN General Assembly Resolution Asymmetry
description: Between 2015-2024, the UN General Assembly passed more resolutions condemning Israel than all other countries combined. States with large-scale atrocities (Syria, China/Xinjiang, North Korea) received a fraction of the attention. This asymmetry in institutional focus is consistent with a causal attribution pattern where Israel is treated as the privileged explanatory variable for regional instability.
source: UN Watch annual reports; UNGA resolution databases

title: Iran's Post-1979 Strategic Misallocation
description: After the 1979 revolution, Iran adopted anti-Zionism as a constitutional organizing principle. Subsequent decades show systematic strategic misallocation: funding Hezbollah and Hamas at enormous cost while domestic infrastructure deteriorated, framing internal dissent as Zionist-linked, and misreading regional dynamics (e.g., the Arab Spring) through an Israel-centric lens. Iran's geopolitical position arguably weakened relative to what realist analysis would have predicted for a state of its resources.
source: Takeyh, R. 'Guardians of the Revolution'; Sadjadpour, K. 'Reading Khamenei'; IISS Strategic Surveys

title: Comparative Ethno-National State Formation
description: Multiple states founded on ethno-national or ethno-religious principles in the same era as Israel (Pakistan 1947, Turkey post-1923 population exchanges, post-colonial African states with ethnic foundations) involved comparable or greater population displacement and ethnic privileging. None face a mainstream political movement dedicated to denying their right to exist as political entities. This asymmetry is difficult to explain from consistent anti-colonial or anti-ethno-nationalist principles alone.
source: Comparative political science literature; Kaufmann, 'Possible and Impossible Solutions to Ethnic Civil Wars'; Abulof, 'The Mortality and Morality of Nations'

title: Soviet Zionology as Causal Attribution Template
description: The Soviet 'Zionology' apparatus (1960s-1980s) explicitly developed anti-Zionism as a framework attributing global capitalist exploitation, Western imperialism, and even internal Soviet problems to Zionist networks. Works like Kichko's 'Judaism Without Embellishment' and the 1983 Anti-Zionist Committee of the Soviet Public illustrate how anti-Zionism was engineered as a causal attribution engine — a structured template for routing explanations of diverse phenomena through a single cause.
source: Korey, W. 'Russian Antisemitism, Pamyat, and the Demonology of Zionism'; Pinkus, B. 'The Soviet Government and the Jews'
